policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere plural simlotayik against ketiv singular simlatek. ASV renders 'put thy raiment upon thee'; English 'raiment' is a collective mass noun that carries no number, and nothing else in the verse counts the garments. No ASV note is mapped here. The English does not distinguish the readings.

Qere weyaradt against ketiv wyrdty, the archaic second feminine singular perfect spelling of the same verb and person. ASV 'and get thee down to the threshing-floor' is second person feminine singular on either reading, and no ASV note is mapped here. The English does not distinguish them.

Qere weshakabt against ketiv wskbty, the archaic second feminine singular spelling of the same perfect. ASV 'and lay thee down' addresses Ruth in the second person on either reading, and no ASV note is mapped here. The English does not distinguish them.

ASV reads 'All that thou sayest I will do', with no 'unto me' rendering the qere elay, and the note mapped to this unit classes as textual_variant and gives 'Another reading is, sayest unto me' as the alternative. The ASV text therefore follows the ketiv, which omits the word, and relegates the qere to the margin.

The ketiv adds 'im, which would make the clause conditional or concessive. ASV renders a flat assertion, 'And now it is true that I am a near kinsman', with no 'if' or 'although' and no italicized supply, and follows it with 'howbeit' for the adversative. That wording reflects the qere, which omits the particle.

Qere margelotayw against ketiv margeloto, plural and singular of a noun meaning the place of the feet. ASV 'And she lay at his feet' is the ordinary rendering of either form, since the English plural translates the lemma's sense rather than its number, and no ASV note is mapped here.

Qere beterem against ketiv btrwm, a purely orthographic difference in the spelling of the same particle. ASV 'before one could discern another' renders the identical word on either reading, and no ASV note is mapped here.

ASV reads 'for he said, Go not empty unto thy mother-in-law', with no 'to me' rendering the qere elay, and the note mapped to this unit classes as textual_variant and gives 'Another reading is, said to me' as the alternative. The ASV text therefore follows the ketiv, which omits the word.
